rows.title: Build a Mindblowing 3D Portfolio Website // Three.js Beginner’s Tutorial

steps.instruction: Run `npm init @vitejs/app` in the terminal, set a project name, select the `vanilla` framework, and choose `JavaScript`.
steps.today: The `@vitejs/app` initializer is deprecated; run `npm create vite@latest` (or `npm init vite`) instead to scaffold the project, then select `Vanilla` and `JavaScript`.

steps.instruction: Install Three.js by running `npm install three` in the project directory.
steps.today: Running `npm install three` remains the standard and officially documented method for installing Three.js via npm.

steps.instruction: Open `index.html` and add `<canvas id="bg"></canvas>` inside the `<body>` preceding the script tag.
steps.today: Manually placing `<canvas id="bg"></canvas>` inside the `<body>` before the script tag is still fully supported HTML for binding a Three.js WebGL renderer.

steps.instruction: Open `style.css` and style `canvas` with `position: fixed; top: 0; left: 0;`.
steps.today: Styling the canvas element with `position: fixed; top: 0; left: 0;` remains standard CSS to anchor a full-window background canvas.

steps.instruction: In `main.js`, import Three.js and initialize the Scene, PerspectiveCamera, and WebGLRenderer bound to the `#bg` canvas.
steps.today: Initializing a `THREE.Scene`, `THREE.PerspectiveCamera`, and passing a canvas element selector to `THREE.WebGLRenderer({ canvas })` remains standard in Three.js.

steps.instruction: Create a Torus geometry and material, combine them into a `THREE.Mesh`, and add the mesh to the scene.
steps.today: Creating geometry with `THREE.TorusGeometry`, pairing it with a material in a `THREE.Mesh`, and adding it to the scene functions the same way.

steps.instruction: Set up a game loop by defining an `animate` function that calls `requestAnimationFrame(animate)` and re-renders the scene.
steps.today: Setting up an `animate` loop with `requestAnimationFrame(animate)` and calling `renderer.render(scene, camera)` still works, though Three.js also provides `renderer.setAnimationLoop()`.

steps.instruction: Add a `PointLight` and an `AmbientLight` to illuminate the 3D objects across the scene.
steps.today: Instantiating `THREE.PointLight` and `THREE.AmbientLight` and adding them to illuminate objects across the scene remains standard practice.

steps.instruction: Import `OrbitControls` from `three/examples/jsm/controls/OrbitControls` and instantiate it with the camera and renderer DOM element.
steps.today: Import `OrbitControls` from `three/addons/controls/OrbitControls.js` instead of the legacy `three/examples/jsm/...` path.

steps.instruction: Create an `addStar` function using `THREE.MathUtils.randFloatSpread` to randomly populate outer space with sphere meshes.
steps.today: `THREE.MathUtils.randFloatSpread` remains a standard Three.js utility function to generate random numbers centered around zero for object placement.

steps.instruction: Load space and celestial body images using `THREE.TextureLoader().load()` to set background and object textures.
steps.today: Instantiating `new THREE.TextureLoader().load()` continues to be the standard method for asynchronously loading image textures onto materials or scene backgrounds.

steps.instruction: Create a `moveCamera` function mapped to `document.body.onscroll` to recalculate scroll offset and update camera and object positions.
steps.today: Binding a custom camera transformation function to `document.body.onscroll` remains valid JavaScript and Three.js practice for scroll-driven camera manipulation.
